newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Japan envoy says PM won't raise Timor issue.
newsitem.headline: Japan envoy says PM won't raise Timor issue.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto will not raise the East Timor issue during his visit to Indonesia this week, Tokyo's Ambassador to Jakarta said on Tuesday.
Hashimoto is due to arrive in Jakarta from Kuala Lumpur on Thursday and leave for Vietnam on Saturday as part of a five-nation tour of Southeast Asian nations.
Exiled Timor sovereignty activist and Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos Horta had urged Hashimoto to broach the subject of human rights abuses in East Timor during his talks with President Suharto.
However, asked whether the issue would be raised in the talks, ambassador Taizo Watanabe said: "Not from our side, no."

Answering questions at a news briefing ahead of Hashimoto's visit, the ambassador also noted that neither the prime minister nor Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda had found time to meet Horta during his visit to Tokyo.

"We are not asking Japan to impose economic sanctions against Indonesia...but there is no conflict between having economic relations with a country...and being very forceful in raising the issue of human rights," Horta told a Tokyo news conference on Monday.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, meanwhile, rejected any suggestion of negotiating with Horta over East Timor.
Speaking during a Foreign Ministry review of the past year on Tuesday, Alatas said Horta represented "only himself and a very small group".

"Ramos Horta is just a charlatan, he is a fraud, he is very clever, he is very vocal, he has succeeded in getting the support of NGOs (non-governmental organisations)...but that doesn't change his intrinsic value in our eyes," the minister said.
Indonesia has bitterly criticised the award of the 1996 Nobel Peace prize to the self-exiled Horta, co-recipient with East Timorese Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo.

Indonesian troops took over East Timor in December 1975 and the former Portuguese colony was incorporated as Indonesia's 27th province the following July in a move still not recognised by the United Nations.
Alatas said Indonesia had the support of much of the world on East Timor, and that the correct place for dialogue over the issue was the United Nations.

Ambassador Watanabe said Japan "fully understands the position of the Indonesian government, but we hope talks and a process of dialogue...will be carried out so this issue can be successfully resolved".
